Ministers resume cabinet talks

Ministers reassembled on Tuesday to consider the terms on which the government may proceed with its programme.

A spokesman said the discussions had been constructive and would continue into the week.

Senior officials confirmed that all parties had reached a preliminary agreement on the key points of contention, though formal announcements were expected only after further consultations later in the day.

The cabinet secretary briefed journalists on the broad outlines of the talks, emphasising that the prime minister remained committed to delivering on the government's manifesto pledges before the end of the parliamentary session.

Opposition spokespeople questioned whether the discussions would produce concrete outcomes, pointing to previous rounds of talks that ended without resolution. Government sources dismissed these concerns as politically motivated.
